To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the COMT × DRD2 interaction modulates gray matter volume and functional connectivity in a similar pattern and that the functional connectivity is negatively correlated with gray matter volume.
genetic variations in the COMT and DR2 genes interact with each other to modulate the structural and functional properties in the brain.

the interactions of genetic variants can generate multiple sub-groups with different levels of the dopamine signaling, which can modulate the brain gray matter volume (a structural property of the brain) and resting-state brain functional connectivity (a functional property of the brain).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to investigating the interaction effects of COMT/DRD2 on brain properties and its functional compensatory mechanism.
the interactions of COMT (rs4680) and DRD2 (rs1800497) on GMV and rsFCS in young healthy adults.
the interactions of genetic variants and their modulation effects on brain properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dopamine signaling modulates the brain structure and function in a non-linear and interactive way.
the dopamine system has an inverted U-shaped modulation on the brain gray matter volume, while the rsFC between brain regions is modulated by dopamine signaling in a U-shaped manner.
the COMT × DRD2 interaction can generate multiple subtypes of individuals with different levels of dopaminergic signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
different genotypic combinations can generate multiple sub-groups with different levels of dopaminergic signaling.

dopamine system can modulate brain properties through different mechanisms and that the interaction of the dopamine system may provide an alternative explanation for the inverse relationship between brain structural and functional properties.

different genetic variations of COMT and/or DRD2 can result in multiple subgroups of young healthy adults with different levels of dopaminergic activity, and the modulation pattern of the dopamine system can be investigated by the interactions of COMT × DRD2 on the GMV and functional connectivity of the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interactions of genetic variants may reveal the inverse modulation patterns of the brain properties in response to the dopamine system, which is a promising direction for future research.
the dopamine system may have different modulation effects on the structural and functional properties.
the dopamine system modulates brain structure and function in an inverse manner.
